If all four agree, output that shared color; otherwise output interior background color. This exactly explains demo4: marker vectors [1,1,7,7], [1,1,7,7], [6,8,8,6], [6,8,8,6], [7,7,3,3], [7,7,3,3], giving outputs [1,9,7], [9,9,9], [9,8,9], [9,9,9], [7,9,3]. The inferred rule gives [[7,0,2],[0,0,0],[6,0,5]], submitted twice and incorrect. Other attempted outputs [7,7,2,2] etc wrong. Therefore likely additional criterion/track grouping needed; preserve contradiction and request demos early. Demo1 output 4x2, demo2 3x2 despite marker rows varying; demo3 6x4; demo4 5x3. Infer output dimensions from number of separator bands and count/selection of marked columns, not blindly all grid compartments. Study which intersections count as active tracks and whether only tracks with non-background marker cells or outer grouping matter. In demo4 all 4 vertical intersection tracks carry non-base colors in some horizontal bands; output width3 adjacency explains. In test, c21/c25 markers 2 then disappear to base5; maybe such varying tracks are not both selected as expected.''')
print(m)
